response.message:
Judge growth by whether the right users experience lasting product value—not just whether acquisition or a headline number rises. Track retention, user value and engagement, and whether growth comes from a repeatable engine; use quantitative and qualitative signals together. [S2] [S3] [S6] [S7] [S11]

## Retention and sustained use

Track retention over time—for example, the percentage still using the product on day 7, 30, and 90—and whether the retention curve flattens or users keep dropping away. Retention is described as the ultimate test of whether the market is actually using the product; a survey can be an earlier signal, but is not a substitute for that test.

[S1] [S3]

## Whether users get must-have value

Measure whether users reach the product’s value and whether the right users would be very disappointed if they could no longer use it. Sean Ellis presents that “very disappointed” response as a leading indicator of product-market fit, useful even with an MVP; the goal is to get more of the right people to experience that value, not simply acquire more users. Pair metrics with conversations or qualitative feedback to understand whether people like the product and what gets in their way.

[S2] [S3] [S1]

## Growth quality and business impact

Track business measures such as revenue, DAU, and acquisition, but test whether a rising number means the product is working. Distinguish vanity milestones from progress in a core growth engine that can be invested in and improved. Consider customer impact and qualitative feedback too; not every worthwhile outcome is best judged by an A/B test or a precise number.

[S5] [S6] [S11]

## Choosing and interpreting measures

Use measures that fit your product and business: NPS is one possible option, but the right way to assess whether users stay or like the product may take more work. Try measuring fuzzy outcomes and learn from the attempt. For products or features, monitor growth curves and diminishing returns; these can help show when an area is maturing and another growth driver may be needed. This is a synthesis of the measurement recommendations, not a single prescribed scorecard.
